tagline: Read Stripe billing streams and safely plan customer write actions.

global_flags.name: credential
global_flags.summary: Credential name to use for the Stripe request.

global_flags.name: connection
global_flags.summary: Credential name alias used only when --credential is omitted; does not resolve pm connections.

global_flags.name: config
global_flags.summary: Connector config override as key=value; never pass secret values here.

global_flags.name: limit
global_flags.summary: Maximum records to emit from stream commands.

global_flags.name: plan
global_flags.summary: Execute an approved reverse-ETL plan by id.

global_flags.name: preview
global_flags.summary: Preview a reverse-ETL write command without making a network mutation.

global_flags.name: approval-token-stdin
global_flags.summary: Read the approval token as one bounded line from standard input.

global_flags.name: confirm
global_flags.summary: Typed confirmation challenge for destructive reverse-ETL writes.

commands.summary: Read Stripe customers through the declared ETL stream.
Plan creation of a Stripe customer through reverse ETL.
commands.risk: Creates customer data in Stripe; requires reverse ETL plan, preview, explicit approval, then execute.
commands.approval: Plan first, inspect preview output, then run only with the generated approval token.
examples: pm stripe customers create --credential stripe-prod --email fixture@example.com --name 'Fixture Customer' --preview --json

commands.summary: Plan an update to a Stripe customer through reverse ETL.
commands.risk: Mutates customer data in Stripe; requires reverse ETL plan, preview, explicit approval, then execute.
commands.approval: Plan first, inspect preview output, then run only with the generated approval token.
examples: pm stripe customers update --credential stripe-prod --id cus_fixture_1 --email updated-fixture@example.com --preview --json

commands.summary: Plan deletion of a Stripe customer with typed destructive confirmation and customer ID redaction.
commands.risk: Destructive Stripe customer deletion; redacts the customer ID from previews and write errors; requires reverse ETL plan, preview, explicit approval, and --confirm destructive before execute.
commands.approval: Plan first, inspect preview output, then run only with the generated approval token and typed --confirm destructive challenge.
examples: pm stripe customers delete --credential stripe-prod --id cus_fixture_delete_1 --preview --json

help_topics.name: destructive-confirmation
help_topics.summary: Stripe DELETE/destructive operations are in scope only through typed destructive confirmation and the reverse ETL plan → preview → approval → execute path.
